verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.156
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 5.156

verses.pali: 16. Saddhammavagga
verses.english: 16. The True Teaching

verses.pali: Tatiyasaddhammasammosasutta
verses.english: The Decline of the True Teaching (3rd)

verses.pali: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Katame pañca?
verses.english: What five?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū duggahitaṁ suttantaṁ pariyāpuṇanti dunnikkhittehi padabyañjanehi.
verses.english: It’s when the mendicants memorize discourses that they learned incorrectly, with misplaced words and phrases.

verses.pali: Dunnikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi dunnayo hoti.
verses.english: When the words and phrases are misplaced, the meaning is misinterpreted.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the first thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dubbacā honti, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, the mendicants are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the second thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te na sakkaccaṁ suttantaṁ paraṁ vācenti;
verses.english: Furthermore, the mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—don’t carefully make others recite the discourses.

verses.pali: tesaṁ accayena chinnamūlako suttanto hoti appaṭisaraṇo.
verses.english: When they pass away, the discourses are cut off at the root, with no-one to preserve them.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the third thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū bāhulikā honti sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: Furthermore, the senior mendicants are indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

verses.pali: Tesaṁ pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: Those who come after them follow their example.

verses.pali: Sāpi hoti bāhulikā sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: They too are indulgent and slack …

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the fourth thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, saṅgho bhinno hoti.
verses.english: Furthermore, there’s a schism in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: Saṅghe kho pana, bhikkhave, bhinne aññamaññaṁ akkosā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ paribhāsā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ parikkhepā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ pariccajanā ca honti.
verses.english: When the Saṅgha is split, they abuse, insult, block, and forsake each other.

verses.pali: Tattha appasannā ceva nappasīdanti, pasannānañca ekaccānaṁ aññathattaṁ hoti.
verses.english: This doesn’t inspire confidence in those without it, and it causes some with confidence to change their minds.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the fifth thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: These five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Katame pañca?
verses.english: What five?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suggahitaṁ suttantaṁ pariyāpuṇanti sunikkhittehi padabyañjanehi.
verses.english: It’s when the mendicants memorize discourses that have been learned correctly, with well placed words and phrases.

verses.pali: Sunikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi sunayo hoti.
verses.english: When the words and phrases are well organized, the meaning is correctly interpreted.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the first thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suvacā honti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, khamā padakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, the mendicants are easy to admonish, having qualities that make them easy to admonish. They’re patient, and take instruction respectfully.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the second thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te sakkaccaṁ suttantaṁ paraṁ vācenti;
verses.english: Furthermore, the mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—carefully make others recite the discourses.

verses.pali: tesaṁ accayena na chinnamūlako suttanto hoti sappaṭisaraṇo.
verses.english: When they pass away, the discourses aren’t cut off at the root, and they have someone to preserve them.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the third thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū na bāhulikā honti na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā; vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: Furthermore, the senior mendicants are not indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion. They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

verses.pali: Tesaṁ pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: Those who come after them follow their example.

verses.pali: Sāpi hoti na bāhulikā na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā, vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: They too are not indulgent or slack …

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the fourth thing …

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, saṅgho samaggo sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeso phāsuṁ viharati.
verses.english: Furthermore, the Saṅgha lives comfortably, in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, with one recitation.

verses.pali: Saṅghe kho pana, bhikkhave, samagge na ceva aññamaññaṁ akkosā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ paribhāsā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ parikkhepā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ pariccajanā honti.
verses.english: When the Saṅgha is in harmony, they don’t abuse, insult, block, or forsake each other.

verses.pali: Tattha appasannā ceva pasīdanti, pasannānañca bhiyyobhāvo hoti.
verses.english: This inspires confidence in those without it, and increases confidence in those who have it.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the fifth thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
verses.english: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
